habitat: Usually in pairs, walking through grassland, bushveld or savanna at all altitudes. It roosts and breeds on top of thorn trees. It sometimes runs a short distance with spread wings and may soar.
summary: A common resident. A large, long-legged grey-and-black bird with long, loose black feathers projecting behind the head. The adult face is orange. The identification line also says red or orange. The immature face is yellow. The flight feathers, upper legs and tail tip are black, and the legs are pink. It is normally silent, but sometimes utters a frog-like croak. The Kemp name Secretarybird and the code VB were left unchanged.

calls.description: Normally silent, but it sometimes utters a frog-like croak. No grade A recording was found. The highest-ranked playable file is a grade B nestling begging call from near Bloemfontein. A grade B Kruger recording is courtship at a nest and is not typed as a call, so it was not selected. The filename is XC505982-Secretarybird_LeeuwrandBFN_19881018.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so all twelve months are listed. The face is orange in the description and red or orange on the identification line. No grade A recording was found. The selected file is a nestling begging call, not the adult croak. A grade B recording from Kruger is courtship at a nest and is not typed as a call. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
